proofs.proof_tex:
Write \(c_{a,P}\), \(\gamma_{a,P}\), and \(h_{a,P,n}\) when dependence on the row law matters, and let \(L_{a,P}=\mathsf Z_{a,\theta,P}/f_{a,P}\).  In the uniform part of the proof, every supremum is over gamma-separated \(P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm S}\), heavy arms, and schedules satisfying \(\text{lem:boundary-likelihood}\).  We prove
\[
\sup_{P,a}d_{\mathrm{BL}}\!\left(
\mathcal L_P\!\left[
\left\{\frac n{h_{a,P,n}}
\bigl(\widehat q_a^{\mathrm{bc}}(\tau)-q_{a,P}(\tau)\bigr)\right\}_{\tau\in\mathcal T}
\right],\mathcal L_P(L_{a,P})\right)\longrightarrow0.
\tag{H1}
\]

By \(\text{ass:hall}\), uniformly in the displayed domain,
\(F_{a,P}^{\pi}(t)=c_{a,P}t^{\gamma_{a,P}-1}\{1+O(t^{\rho_{a,P}})\}\), with \(c_{a,P}\), \(\rho_{a,P}\), and the validity threshold bounded away from zero and infinity as appropriate.  Substitution in the definition of \(t_{a,P,n}\), followed by monotonicity of the distribution function, gives
\[
\sup_{P,a}\left|c_{a,P}n t_{a,P,n}^{\gamma_{a,P}}-1\right|\longrightarrow0,
\qquad
h_{a,P,n}=(c_{a,P}n)^{1/\gamma_{a,P}}\{1+o(1)\}.
\tag{H2}
\]
Since \(1+\epsilon_\gamma\le\gamma_{a,P}\le2-\epsilon_\gamma\) on the heavy domain, \(h_{a,P,n}/n\to0\) uniformly.

Put \(Z_{i,P}=h_{a,P,n}\pi_{a,P}(X_i)\) and \(U_{i,P}=\Psi_{a,P}(Y_i)\) on \(\{A_i=a\}\).  By \(\text{ass:consistency}\) and \(\text{ass:unconfoundedness}\), conditionally on \(X_i\), this event has probability \(\pi_{a,P}(X_i)\), and its outcome mark has the potential-outcome conditional law.  Thus, for every continuous \(g\) supported on a compact \(z\)-annulus, a Stieltjes change of variables, (H2), and \(\text{lem:score-law-factorization}\) give
\[
\begin{split}
&nE_P\!\left[\mathbf1\{A_i=a\}g(Z_{i,P},U_{i,P})\right]\\
&\quad\longrightarrow
\int_0^\infty\!\int_{\mathbb R^R}g(z,u)H_{a,P}(du)
(\gamma_{a,P}-1)z^{\gamma_{a,P}-1}\,dz
\end{split}
\tag{H3}
\]
uniformly.  The Hall error is uniform after scaling by \(h_{a,P,n}\), and the mark error is at most \(R\omega_{\mathrm{mark}}(z/h_{a,P,n})\), which tends uniformly to zero on such annuli.  For nonnegative \(g\), \(\text{ass:iid}\) gives the exact identity
\[
E_P\exp\!\left\{-\sum_{i=1}^n\mathbf1\{A_i=a\}g(Z_{i,P},U_{i,P})\right\}
=\left[1-E_P\{\mathbf1(A_i=a)(1-e^{-g(Z_{i,P},U_{i,P})})\}\right]^n.
\tag{H4}
\]
Using \(n\log(1-x_n)=-nx_n+o(1)\) whenever \(nx_n=O(1)\), (H3)--(H4) prove uniform convergence of the marked point process on compact annuli.

Define the population-clipped oracle score
\[
S_{a,P,n}(\tau)=\frac1{h_{a,P,n}}\sum_{i=1}^n
\frac{\mathbf1\{A_i=a\}\psi_{a,\tau}(Y_i)}
{\pi_{a,P}(X_i)\vee b_{a,P,n}}.
\tag{H5}
\]
Applying (H4) to truncations of \(u_\tau/\max\{z,\theta_a\}\), subtracting their expectations, and then removing the truncations gives
\[
S_{a,P,n}-E_PS_{a,P,n}\ \Longrightarrow_{\mathrm{unif}}\ \mathsf Z_{a,\theta,P}.
\tag{H6}
\]
The removal is uniform.  Above \(z=C\), the centered second moment is at most
\[
C_1\int_C^\infty z^{\gamma_{a,P}-3}\,dz\le C_2C^{-\epsilon_\gamma}.
\]
Below \(z=c\), the probability of any point is at most
\[
C_3\int_0^c z^{\gamma_{a,P}-1}\,dz\le C_4c^{1+\epsilon_\gamma},
\]
and the magnitude of the omitted compensator is bounded by a constant times
\(\int_0^c z^{\gamma_{a,P}-2}dz\le Cc^{\epsilon_\gamma}\).  These inequalities also give uniform tightness, including \(\theta_a=0\).

By the quantile definition and iterated expectation,
\(E_Pm_{a,\tau}(X)=E_P\psi_{a,\tau}\{Y(a)\}=0\).  Hence only clipping contributes to the mean.  Hall integration and \(\text{ass:tail-marks}\) imply
\[
\begin{split}
E_PS_{a,P,n}(\tau)
&=\frac n{h_{a,P,n}}E_P\!\left[m_{a,\tau}(X)
\left\{\frac{\pi_a(X)}{\pi_a(X)\vee\theta_a/h_{a,P,n}}-1\right\}\right]\\
&\longrightarrow m^{\mathrm{tail}}_{a,\tau}(\gamma_{a,P}-1)
\int_0^{\theta_a}(z/\theta_a-1)z^{\gamma_{a,P}-2}\,dz\\
&=-\frac{\theta_a^{\gamma_{a,P}-1}}{\gamma_{a,P}}
m^{\mathrm{tail}}_{a,\tau}=\mu_{a,\theta,P}(\tau),
\end{split}
\tag{H7}
\]
uniformly, with value zero when \(\theta_a=0\).  The last equality follows by integrating the two powers separately; it establishes the stated positive correction sign without altering the causal target.

The count sandwich obtained from the punctured relative-error bound in \(\text{lem:boundary-likelihood}\), together with (H2), yields
\[
\frac{\widehat h_{a,n}}{h_{a,P,n}}\to_P1,
\qquad
h_{a,P,n}\widehat p_{a,(\lceil\widehat h_{a,n}\rceil)}\to_P1,
\qquad
\widehat h_{a,n}\widehat b_{a,n}\to_P\vartheta_a=\theta_a
\tag{H8}
\]
uniformly.  To transfer the score, split at \(u_{a,n}=M_n/h_{a,P,n}\).  The reciprocal identity and the definition of \(D_{a,n}\) give
\[
\begin{split}
\max_{\tau\in\mathcal T}|S^{\mathrm{fe}}_{a,P,n}(\tau)-S_{a,P,n}(\tau)|
&\le CE_{a,n}\frac1{h_{a,P,n}}\sum_{i=1}^n
\frac{\mathbf1\{A_i=a,\ \pi_a(X_i)\le M_n/h_{a,P,n}\}}
{\pi_a(X_i)\vee b_{a,P,n}}\\
&\quad+\max_{\tau\in\mathcal T}|D_{a,n}(\tau)|+o_P(1).
\end{split}
\tag{H9}
\]
Hall integration bounds the normalized sum by \(O_P(M_n^{\gamma_{a,P}-1})\), uniformly.  Therefore the two conclusions of \(\text{lem:boundary-likelihood}\), in particular
\(E_{a,n}M_n^{\gamma_{a,P}-1}=o_P(1)\), make (H9) \(o_P(1)\).  The relative-error square-integral conclusion of the same lemma transfers the local curvature term.

For completeness, checking the three possible sign configurations of \(e\) and \(e-v\) gives Knight's exact identity
\[
\rho_\tau(e-v)-\rho_\tau(e)
=-v\{\tau-\mathbf1(e\le0)\}
+\int_0^v\{\mathbf1(e\le s)-\mathbf1(e\le0)\}\,ds.
\tag{H10}
\]
Use \(e=Y_i-q_a(\tau)\) and \(v=th_{a,P,n}/n\).  Conditional expectation, \(\text{ass:conditional-density-modulus}\), and the Hall bound on the clipped covariate set imply, uniformly for bounded \(t\) and \(\tau\in\mathcal T\),
\[
E_P\{\text{scaled Knight remainder}\}=\frac12f_{a,P}(\tau)t^2+o(1).
\tag{H11}
\]
The centered remainder has variance at most \(C|t|^3h_{a,P,n}/n=o(1)\) by (H2).  Consequently,
\[
\widehat Q_{a,n,\tau}(t)
=\frac12f_{a,P}(\tau)t^2
-t\{\mathsf Z_{a,\theta,P}(\tau)+\mu_{a,\theta,P}(\tau)\}+o_P(1)
\tag{H12}
\]
in uniform bounded-Lipschitz approximation, jointly over the finite set \(\mathcal T\).

It remains to verify that the correction is empirical.  If
\(t_{a,k}=F_{a,P}^{\pi,-1}(k_n/n)\), uniform Hall inversion gives
\[
t_{a,k}\asymp(k_n/n)^{1/(\gamma_{a,P}-1)},
\qquad
nP\{A=a,\pi_a(X)\le t_{a,k}\}\asymp k_nt_{a,k}\to\infty.
\tag{H13}
\]
The tail-count sandwich and integration of the empirical tail survival function then give
\(\widehat\gamma_a-\gamma_{a,P}=o_P(1)\).  Equation (H13), \(\text{ass:tail-marks}\), and the inner-fold version of the convex argument following (H12) give
\[
\max_{\tau\in\mathcal T}|\widehat m^{\mathrm{tail}}_{a,\tau}-m^{\mathrm{tail}}_{a,\tau}|=o_P(1).
\]
For the density estimator, the weighted denominator divided by \(n\) converges to one, while its kernel numerator has expectation \(f_{a,P}(\tau)+o(1)\) by \(\text{ass:conditional-density-modulus}\).  Its variance is bounded by
\[
\frac C{n\omega_{a,n}}E_P\!\left[
\frac{\pi_a(X)}{\{\pi_a(X)\vee b_{a,P,n}\}^2}\right]
\le\frac{Ch_{a,P,n}^{2-\gamma_{a,P}}}{n\omega_{a,n}}
\le\frac{Ch_{a,P,n}}{n\omega_{a,n}}=o(1).
\tag{H14}
\]
The common density modulus supplies a uniform upper bound at every target quantile: choose fixed \(v_0>0\) at which the modulus is at most one and integrate the resulting lower bound over \([q_a(\tau)-v_0,q_a(\tau)+v_0]\).  Together with \(\text{ass:quantile-density}\), this makes every division by \(f_{a,P}\) uniform.  Also
\(|\widehat q_a-q_a|/\omega_{a,n}=O_P\{h_{a,P,n}/(n\omega_{a,n})\}=o_P(1)\).  Therefore
\[
\widehat f_a-f_{a,P}=o_P(1),
\qquad
\widehat\mu_{a,\theta}-\mu_{a,\theta,P}=o_P(1)
\tag{H15}
\]
uniformly.

The curvature in (H12) is bounded below by \(\text{ass:quantile-density}\).  Comparing the convex objective at the unique quadratic minimizer and at points a fixed distance on either side shows that its smallest minimizer is uniformly tight and satisfies
\[
\frac n{h_{a,P,n}}(\widehat q_a-q_{a,P})
\ \Longrightarrow_{\mathrm{unif}}\
\frac{\mathsf Z_{a,\theta,P}+\mu_{a,\theta,P}}{f_{a,P}}.
\tag{H16}
\]
Subtracting the empirical correction in \(\text{def:drift-correction}\) and using (H8) and (H15) proves (H1).  With a fixed \(P\), the same equations use law-specific constants and require only \(1<\gamma_a<2\), proving the fixed-law corollary.  Replacing the estimated propensity and clip by their population versions removes (H8)--(H9) and proves oracle recovery.  Finally, \(\text{lem:score-law-factorization}\) shows that (H3), and hence the Lévy law, depends on the endpoint outcome only through \(H_{a,P}\).

Fix a finite-variance arm and write \(q_{a,P}\), \(f_{a,P}\), and \(\mathrm{IF}_{a,P}\).  Let \(L_{a,P}\) be centered Gaussian with covariance
\[
\Sigma_{a,P}=E_P\!\left[
\{\mathrm{IF}_{a,P}(O;\tau)\}_{\tau\in\mathcal T}
\{\mathrm{IF}_{a,P}(O;\tau)\}_{\tau\in\mathcal T}^{\top}
\right].
\tag{G1}
\]
All suprema below are over the explicitly scheduled gamma-separated Gaussian domain in the statement.

For a log-propensity direction \(g\), direct differentiation of the Bernoulli log likelihood gives
\[
s_g(O)=\frac{\{\mathbf1(A=a)-\pi_a(X)\}g(X)}{1-\pi_a(X)},
\qquad
\mathcal I_{a,P}(g_1,g_2)=E_P\!\left[
\frac{\pi_a(X)}{1-\pi_a(X)}g_1(X)g_2(X)\right].
\tag{G2}
\]
The derivative of the signed functional in direction \(g\) is
\(\dot\Lambda_{a,P}(g)=E_P\{m_{a,\tau}(X)g(X)\}\).  Its information-space Riesz representer is
\[
r_{a,\tau,P}(X)=m_{a,\tau}(X)\frac{1-\pi_a(X)}{\pi_a(X)},
\tag{G3}
\]
because substituting (G3) into (G2) gives
\(\mathcal I_{a,P}(r_{a,\tau,P},g)=\dot\Lambda_{a,P}(g)\).  Positivity licenses the divisions, and
\[
E_Ps_{r_{a,\tau,P}}^2
=E_P\!\left[m_{a,\tau}(X)^2\frac{1-\pi_a(X)}{\pi_a(X)}\right]
\le C_{\mathrm G}
\tag{G4}
\]
by \(\text{ass:finite-variance}\) and \(|m_{a,\tau}|\le1\).

Let \(r_{a,\tau,P,J}\) be the information projection of (G3) on the likelihood sieve.  On the cell at distance of order \(j/J\) from the endpoint, \(\text{ass:boundary-link}\), the local support and normalization of the B-splines, and \(\text{ass:holder}\) give, after summing the cellwise powers,
\[
\|s_{r_{a,\tau,P,J}}-s_{r_{a,\tau,P}}\|_{L^2(P)}=o(1)
\tag{G5}
\]
uniformly when \(2<\gamma_{a,P}<\infty\), equivalently \(0<\alpha_{a,P}<1\).  The same calculation and the likelihood score equation yield
\[
\sqrt n\,|\text{product approximation bias}|\le C\sqrt nJ_n^{-2s},
\qquad
\sqrt n\,|\text{reciprocal quadratic remainder}|
=O_P(J_n^{\alpha_{a,P}}/\sqrt n),
\tag{G6}
\]
and empirical-Hessian replacement error
\[
O_P\!\left\{\frac{J_n^{\alpha_{a,P}+1}\log n}{n}\right\}^{1/2}=o_P(1).
\tag{G7}
\]
Every term is \(o_P(1)\) by the displayed schedules.  If \(\gamma_{a,P}=\infty\), then \(\pi_a=\exp(g_a)\) and the fixed Hölder radius gives \(\inf_x\pi_a(x)\ge e^{-C}>0\).  Profiling the additional \(\log d_a\) direction against the quasi-uniform spline space gives a residual of squared norm \(O(J_n^{-1})\), a profiled coefficient error \(O_P(\sqrt{J_n/n})\), maximum sample residual \(O_P\{\log(n/J_n)\}\), and profiled spline-function supremum error
\[
O_P\!\left\{\sqrt{J_n\log J_n/n}+J_n^{-s}\right\}.
\tag{G8}
\]
Thus \(J_n\log n/n\to0\) and \(J_n^{-s}\log(n/J_n)\to0\) give uniform sample-point consistency.  This is the profiled argument already established for the bounded arm in \(\text{prop:finite-variance-sanity}\), with constants uniform over the fixed Hölder ball.

For each fold, (G2)--(G8), the likelihood score equation, and the nonpositive inner product of a concave maximizer's feasible displacement with its normal-cone residual give
\[
\sqrt n\sum_{k=1}^K\frac{|I_k|}{n}
\int m_{a,\tau}(x)
\frac{\widehat\pi_{a,-k}(x)-\pi_a(x)}{\pi_a(x)}\,dP_X(x)
=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n s_{r_{a,\tau,P}}(O_i)+o_P(1).
\tag{G9}
\]
The coefficient is one because every observation is used in \(K-1\) training folds, each of size \(n(K-1)/K+O(1)\).  Conditional on a training fold, cross-fitting makes the centered evaluation error mean zero, and its conditional variance is at most
\[
C\int\frac{(\widehat\pi_{a,-k}-\pi_a)^2}{\pi_a}\,dP_X
=O_P(J_n^{-2s}+J_n^{2\alpha_{a,P}}/n)=o_P(1).
\tag{G10}
\]
For finite \(\gamma_{a,P}>2\), the last conclusion uses \(2\alpha_{a,P}<\alpha_{a,P}+1\); the bounded case uses \(\alpha_{a,P}=0\).

Clipping is first-order negligible.  In the bounded case, (G8) and the common lower bound make it inactive with probability tending uniformly to one.  For finite \(\gamma_{a,P}>2\), introduce only for this proof \(b_{a,P,n}^{\circ}=\vartheta_a/h_{a,P,n}\).  The definition of \(t_{a,P,n}\) and \(\text{ass:hall}\) give \(h_{a,P,n}=(c_{a,P}n)^{1/\gamma_{a,P}}\{1+o(1)\}\); Hall integration then gives
\[
\sqrt n\left|E_Pm_{a,\tau}(X)
\left\{\frac{\pi_a(X)}{\pi_a(X)\vee b_{a,P,n}^{\circ}}-1\right\}\right|
\le Cn^{1/2-(\gamma_{a,P}-1)/\gamma_{a,P}}=o(1)
\tag{G11}
\]
uniformly because \(\gamma_{a,P}\ge2+\epsilon_\gamma\).  Its centered version has variance tending uniformly to zero because Stieltjes integration of \(\text{ass:hall}\) gives
\[
E_P\!\left[\pi_a(X)^{-1}\mathbf1\{\pi_a(X)\le u\}\right]
\le Cu^{\gamma_{a,P}-2}.
\tag{G12}
\]
The count sandwich proves \(\widehat b_{a,n}/b_{a,P,n}^{\circ}\to_P1\) when \(\vartheta_a>0\); when \(\vartheta_a=0\), both thresholds vanish.  This transfers (G11) to the empirical clip.

Applying the exact algebraic identity
\[
\rho_\tau(e-v)-\rho_\tau(e)
=-v\{\tau-\mathbf1(e\le0)\}
+\int_0^v\{\mathbf1(e\le s)-\mathbf1(e\le0)\}\,ds
\]
with \(v=t/\sqrt n\), and using \(\text{ass:conditional-density-modulus}\) and \(\text{ass:quantile-density}\), gives the uniform local expansion
\[
\widehat Q^{\mathrm G}_{a,n,\tau}(t)
=\frac12f_{a,P}(\tau)t^2
-t\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n
\left[
\frac{\mathbf1(A_i=a)\psi_{a,\tau}(Y_i)}{\pi_a(X_i)}
-s_{r_{a,\tau,P}}(O_i)
\right]+o_P(1).
\tag{G13}
\]
By (G3), the bracket is exactly
\[
m_{a,\tau}(X_i)+\frac{\mathbf1(A_i=a)
\{\psi_{a,\tau}(Y_i)-m_{a,\tau}(X_i)\}}{\pi_a(X_i)}
=f_{a,P}(\tau)\mathrm{IF}_{a,P}(O_i;\tau).
\tag{G14}
\]
It is centered by consistency, unconfoundedness, and
\(E_P\psi_{a,\tau}\{Y(a)\}=0\).

It remains to verify the uniform Gaussian approximation.  Since \(\mathcal T\) is finite, (G14), the density lower bound, and \(|m|,|\psi|\le1\) reduce multivariate Lindeberg to the inverse-weight term.  For finite \(\gamma_{a,P}\ge2+\epsilon_\gamma\), (G12) with \(u=x^{-1}\) gives
\[
E_P\!\left[
\frac{\mathbf1(A=a)}{\pi_a(X)^2}
\mathbf1\{\pi_a(X)^{-1}>x\}\right]
=E_P\!\left[\frac1{\pi_a(X)}\mathbf1\{\pi_a(X)<x^{-1}\}\right]
\le Cx^{-(\gamma_{a,P}-2)}\le Cx^{-\epsilon_\gamma}.
\tag{G15}
\]
For \(\gamma_{a,P}=\infty\), the common propensity lower bound makes the summands uniformly bounded.  Taking \(x\) proportional to \(\sqrt n\) proves uniform Lindeberg.  For each fixed coefficient vector, expand the characteristic function of its scalar projection to second order on the Lindeberg-truncated event; the remainder is bounded by the corresponding truncated second moment.  Gaussian smoothing followed by removal of the smoothing converts the resulting characteristic-function approximation into bounded-Lipschitz approximation to the centered Gaussian having row covariance (G1).  No covariance convergence across rows is needed.

Finally, the common lower curvature in (G13) and a two-sided convexity comparison at the quadratic minimizer imply, uniformly over arms and \(\tau\),
\[
\sqrt n\{\widehat q_a(\tau)-q_{a,P}(\tau)\}
=\frac1{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n\mathrm{IF}_{a,P}(O_i;\tau)+o_P(1).
\tag{G16}
\]
The preceding Lindeberg calculation and (G16) prove both uniform assertions in the replacement statement.  Dropping the suprema yields its fixed-law corollary.

For each row law \(P\), define
\[
W_{a,P,n}=\frac n{H_{a,P,n}}
(\widehat q_a^{\mathrm{bc}}-q_{a,P}).
\tag{Q1}
\]
The uniform heavy theorem gives bounded-Lipschitz approximation of every heavy coordinate to \(L_{a,P}\), and the uniform Gaussian theorem gives the corresponding result for every finite-variance coordinate.  For finite \(\gamma_{a,P}>2\), uniform Hall inversion at \(F_{a,P}^{\pi,-1}(k_n/n)\), the fitted-tail count sandwich, and integration of the empirical survival function give \(\widehat\gamma_a-\gamma_{a,P}=o_P(1)\).  If \(\gamma_{a,P}=\infty\), the common Hölder radius makes \(1/\pi_a\) a uniformly bounded equicontinuous family; its upper \(k_n/n\) order-statistic log spacings are therefore \(o_P(1)\), so the Hill reciprocal diverges.  By \(\text{ass:gamma-separation}\),
\[
\sup_PP_P\{\widehat{\mathcal A}_{\mathrm H}\ne\mathcal A_{\mathrm H}\}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{Q2}
\]
On the complement, \(\text{def:drift-correction}\) sets the Gaussian-arm correction to zero, so its Gaussian expansion applies to (Q1).

We next identify the joint law rather than infer it from marginal convergence.  For two heavy arms, \(\text{ass:opposite-overlap}\) gives disjoint endpoint neighborhoods.  For compactly supported nonnegative \(g_0,g_1\), one observation cannot enter both endpoint point processes, and the iid Laplace transform equals
\[
\left[1-\frac{\nu_{0,P,n}(1-e^{-g_0})}{n}
-\frac{\nu_{1,P,n}(1-e^{-g_1})}{n}+o(n^{-1})\right]^n.
\tag{Q3}
\]
The uniform Hall and score-mark limits convert (Q3) into the product of the two limiting Laplace functionals, proving independence of the heavy limits.  With one heavy and one Gaussian arm, truncate the Gaussian summands on the heavy endpoint set.  By \(\text{ass:finite-variance}\) and (G15), the discarded variance tends uniformly to zero.  On a retained heavy endpoint event, binary treatment makes the other arm's residual term vanish, while its regression term is bounded by one.  Thus the one-observation cross term between a compactly supported endpoint transform and the Gaussian exponential is \(O(n^{-3/2})\), and multiplication by \(n\) still makes it vanish.  Hence the joint iid characteristic function factorizes.  With two Gaussian arms, the joint characteristic-function expansion used after (G15) retains the cross block
\(E_P[\mathrm{IF}_{0,P}\mathrm{IF}_{1,P}^{\top}]\).  It follows that
\[
\sup_Pd_{\mathrm{BL}}\!\left(
\mathcal L_P(W_{0,P,n},W_{1,P,n}),
\mathcal L_P(L_{0,P},L_{1,P})
\right)\longrightarrow0.
\tag{Q4}
\]
This calculation proves, rather than assumes, all joint-law clauses used to name \(Z_{P,n}\) in \(\text{def:moving-row-law}\).

The estimator and scale definitions give the exact nonasymptotic identity
\[
\frac n{H_{P,n}}(\widehat\Delta^{\mathrm{bc}}-\Delta_P)
=\ell_{1,P,n}W_{1,P,n}-\ell_{0,P,n}W_{0,P,n}.
\tag{Q5}
\]
Since \(0\le\ell_{a,P,n}\le1\), the linear map in (Q5) has uniformly bounded Lipschitz norm.  Applying it to (Q4) yields
\[
\sup_Pd_{\mathrm{BL}}\!\left(
\mathcal L_P\!\left\{\frac n{H_{P,n}}
(\widehat\Delta^{\mathrm{bc}}-\Delta_P)\right\},
\mathcal L_P(Z_{P,n})
\right)\longrightarrow0,
\tag{Q6}
\]
without any limit assumption on \(\ell_{a,P,n}\).

For a fixed \(P\), the definition of \(t_{a,P,n}\) and \(\text{ass:hall}\) give
\(h_{a,P,n}=(c_{a,P}n)^{1/\gamma_{a,P}}\{1+o(1)\}\).  If two fixed heavy indices differ, the smaller \(\gamma_a\) has the larger normalization and the other coefficient in (Q5) tends to zero.  Equal indices retain the ratio of Hall constants.  Since \(h_{a,P,n}/\sqrt n\to\infty\) for \(\gamma_a<2\), a heavy arm dominates a Gaussian arm.  If both arms are Gaussian, both scales equal \(\sqrt n\), and (Q4) retains their shared covariance.  Therefore, whenever \(\ell_{a,P,n}\to\ell_a\), (Q6) gives
\[
\frac n{H_{P,n}}(\widehat\Delta^{\mathrm{bc}}-\Delta_P)
\Rightarrow\ell_1L_{1,P}-\ell_0L_{0,P}.
\tag{Q7}
\]
This proves every fixed-law phase assertion, while (Q3) proves the stated two-heavy independence.

We prove conditional approximation to the moving law uniformly over the gamma-separated class satisfying the full-sample and refit schedules.  At an arbitrary size \(N\), put
\[
W_{P,N}^{\circ}=
\left\{\frac N{\widehat H_{a,N}}
(\widehat q_{a,N}^{\mathrm{bc}}-q_{a,P})\right\}_{a\in\mathcal A}.
\tag{S1}
\]
The uniform heavy and Gaussian expansions, the scale consistency in \(\text{thm:oracle-preservation}\), and the Hall/order-statistic classification argument in \(\text{thm:joint-qte}\) provide a permutation-symmetric leading statistic \(S_{P,N}\) satisfying, for every \(\varepsilon>0\),
\[
\sup_PP_P\{\|W_{P,N}^{\circ}-S_{P,N}\|>\varepsilon\}\to0,
\qquad
\sup_Pd_{\mathrm{BL}}\{\mathcal L_P(S_{P,N}),\mathcal L_P(L_{0,P},L_{1,P})\}\to0.
\tag{S2}
\]
For \(\gamma=\infty\), classification uses only the common Hölder-ball bound and equicontinuity, so no oracle regime label enters (S1).

Let \(g:\mathbb R^{2R}\to[-1,1]\) be one-Lipschitz and define the complete subsample average
\[
U_{n,m,P}(g)=\binom nm^{-1}\sum_{|b|=m}g(S_{P,b})
=E_B\{g(S_{P,B})\mid O_1,\ldots,O_n\}.
\tag{S3}
\]
Successively subtracting conditional expectations over proper coordinate subsets gives the orthogonal decomposition
\[
g(S_{P,m})-E_Pg(S_{P,m})
=\sum_{j=1}^m\sum_{|C|=j}h_{P,m,j}(O_C),
\tag{S4}
\]
where each \(h_{P,m,j}\) has conditional mean zero given any \(j-1\) arguments.  Put
\(\zeta_{P,m,j}=E_Ph_{P,m,j}(O_1,\ldots,O_j)^2\).  Independence, orthogonality, and counting the \(m\)-subsets containing each fixed \(j\)-subset give
\[
\begin{split}
\operatorname{Var}_P\{U_{n,m,P}(g)\}
&=\sum_{j=1}^m\frac{\binom mj^2}{\binom nj}\zeta_{P,m,j}\\
&\le\frac mn\sum_{j=1}^m\binom mj\zeta_{P,m,j}
=\frac mn\operatorname{Var}_P\{g(S_{P,m})\}
\le4m/n.
\end{split}
\tag{S5}
\]
Here \(\binom mj/\binom nj\le m/n\).  A uniform \(m\)-subset of iid observations has unconditionally the same law as \(m\) iid observations.  Hence (S2)--(S5) imply
\[
U_{n,m,P}(g)-E_Pg(L_{0,P},L_{1,P})\to_P0
\tag{S6}
\]
uniformly in \(P\).

The candidate arm-limit family is uniformly tight: (G4) bounds Gaussian second moments, while the small- and large-\(z\) inequalities following (H6) bound the heavy tails.  On a common compact ball, the unit bounded-Lipschitz class has a finite uniform-norm net.  Applying (S5) to this finite net and using tightness off the ball upgrades (S6) to
\[
\sup_PP_P\!\left\{
d_{\mathrm{BL}}\bigl(\mathcal L_B(S_{P,B}\mid O_1^n),
\mathcal L_P(L_{0,P},L_{1,P})\bigr)>\varepsilon\right\}\to0.
\tag{S7}
\]
The unconditional subsample identity and (S2) also give
\[
\sup_PE_P\mathbb P_B\{\|W_{P,B}^{\circ}-S_{P,B}\|>\varepsilon\mid O_1^n\}\to0.
\tag{S8}
\]
If the inner conditional probability in (S8) is denoted by \(R_{P,n}\), then
\(P_P(R_{P,n}>\eta)\le E_PR_{P,n}/\eta\).  Thus (S7)--(S8) prove conditional uniform convergence of the refitted arm vector.

By \(\text{def:vector-subsampling}\),
\[
V_{B,a}=W_{P,B,a}^{\circ}-C_{B,a},
\qquad
C_{B,a}=\frac m{\widehat H_{a,m,B}}
(\widehat q_{a,n}^{\mathrm{bc}}-q_{a,P}).
\tag{S9}
\]
Uniform tightness in (S2), scale consistency, and the Hall inversion implied by \(\text{ass:hall}\) yield
\[
\|C_{B,a}\|=O_P\!\left(\frac m{H_{a,P,m}}\frac{H_{a,P,n}}n\right)
=\begin{cases}
O_P\{(m/n)^{1-1/\gamma_{a,P}}\},&a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm H},\\
O_P\{(m/n)^{1/2}\},&a\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm G}.
\end{cases}
\tag{S10}
\]
Both are uniformly \(o_P(1)\), since in the heavy case
\(1-1/\gamma_{a,P}\ge\epsilon_\gamma/(1+\epsilon_\gamma)\).  The same scale and classification results give
\(\max_a|\widehat\ell_{a,n}-\ell_{a,P,n}|=o_P(1)\) uniformly.  Recombination has Lipschitz norm at most two, so (S7)--(S10) imply
\[
\sup_PP_P\!\left\{
d_{\mathrm{BL}}\!\left(
\mathcal L_B(T_{B,n}\mid O_1^n),\mathcal L_P(Z_{P,n})
\right)>\varepsilon\right\}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{S11}
\]

Fix \(\tau\in\mathcal T\).  The full-sample approximation (Q6), scale consistency, and (S11) compare the normalized estimation error and the conditional statistic to the same scalar law \(Z_{P,n}(\tau)\).  A piecewise-linear one-Lipschitz approximation to a half-line, rescaled over width \(\eta\), shows that bounded-Lipschitz error \(\delta\) changes a distribution function by at most \(\delta/\eta\) plus the probability of an interval of radius \(\eta\).  Applying \(\text{ass:anti-concentration}\), first letting \(\eta\downarrow0\) and then \(\delta\downarrow0\), gives
\[
\sup_P\left|
P_P\!\left\{
c_{n,\alpha/2}(\tau)\le
\frac n{\widehat H_n}
(\widehat\Delta^{\mathrm{bc}}(\tau)-\Delta_P(\tau))
\le c_{n,1-\alpha/2}(\tau)
\right\}-(1-\alpha)\right|\longrightarrow0.
\tag{S12}
\]
This event is exactly coverage by the interval in the statement.  Finiteness of \(\mathcal T\) permits taking the maximum of the coordinatewise errors, but does not turn the intervals into a simultaneous band.

For fixed \(P\), compactness of \([0,1]^2\) gives a further subsequence on which both recombination weights converge, and (S11) then gives the fixed-law conditional limit.  We finally prove the claimed scope of the counterexample.  In the two-heavy family from \(\text{prop:smooth-inclusion}\), fix an interior \(\gamma\in(1,2)\), equal Hall constants, and nondegenerate convergent endpoint-score laws and densities.  For fixed \(c>0\), let
\[
\gamma_{0,n}=\gamma+\frac c{2\log n},
\qquad
\gamma_{1,n}=\gamma-\frac c{2\log n}.
\tag{S13}
\]
These rows remain gamma-separated.  Hall inversion gives
\[
\log\{h_{0,P_n,n}/h_{1,P_n,n}\}
=\{\gamma_{0,n}^{-1}-\gamma_{1,n}^{-1}\}\log n+o(1)
\longrightarrow-c/\gamma^2.
\tag{S14}
\]
Thus the moving row law retains
\(L_{1,P_n}-e^{-c/\gamma^2}L_{0,P_n}\), whereas holding a row fixed and increasing sample size eliminates its larger-index arm.  Independence and nondegeneracy distinguish these laws: equality of their characteristic functions near zero would force the characteristic function of a nonzero multiple of \(L_{0,P_n}\) to equal one near zero, which would make that component degenerate.

If raw scalar subsampling uses \(m=n^\beta\), \(0<\beta<1\), the same calculation gives
\[
\log\{h_{0,P_n,m}/h_{1,P_n,m}\}\longrightarrow-\beta c/\gamma^2,
\tag{S15}
\]
and hence the wrong mixture \(L_1-e^{-\beta c/\gamma^2}L_0\).  In contrast, (S11) standardizes the refitted arms at their separate \(m\)-scales and recombines them with \(\widehat\ell_{a,n}\), reproducing (S14).  Equations (S13)--(S15) therefore refute only fixed-limit uniformity and raw scalar subsampling, while certifying the moving-law validity of the arm-vector construction.

prose_updates.tldr: A boundary-adapted growing Bernoulli likelihood preserves the compensated infinitely divisible clipped-IPW quantile law uniformly over gamma-separated scheduled rows, while the finite-variance branch admits a uniform learned-propensity Gaussian approximation. The constrained signed Riesz expansion yields the rate \(J_n^{-s}+n^{-1/2}J_n^{(\alpha_a-1)/2}+J_n^{\alpha_a}/n\) and the corrected transfer condition \(E_{a,n}M_n^{\gamma_a-1}=o_P(1)\). The formally defined moving row variable \(Z_{P,n}=\ell_{1,P,n}L_{1,P}-\ell_{0,P,n}L_{0,P}\) combines the arm laws without requiring convergence of the recombination weights, and fully refitted arm-vector subsampling estimates its law uniformly. The separate critical fold-labelled Poisson question is outside these results.

project_justification.gap: The closest weak-overlap QTE theorem uses the observed true propensity. Regular estimated-propensity quantile and series-logit results do not provide the singular Hall-boundary signed-functional expansion, a row-wise uniform learned-propensity limit away from \(\gamma=2\), or inference that remains valid under local \(1/\log n\) changes in the two arm scales.
project_justification.niche: A feasible full-population QTE procedure must preserve signed cancellation at a Hall boundary, use a positive-weight convex argmin and empirical clipping correction, retain the learned-score covariance in regular arms, and approximate the moving two-arm row law rather than force a common fixed limit.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the constrained-sieve log and signed-functional rates, proves the amplified oracle-transfer condition, establishes heavy and Gaussian arm expansions uniformly on their explicit gamma-separated scheduled domains, recombines them into the declared variable \(Z_{P,n}\), and proves uniform conditional validity and pointwise coverage for fully refitted arm-vector subsampling under moving-law anti-concentration.

sampling_model.design: Independent superpopulation sampling under conditional unconfoundedness; identification of \(\Delta(\tau)\) is taken as given, and the contribution is uniform row-wise limit and inference theory.
sampling_model.units: \(O_i=(X_i,A_i,Y_i)\), \(i=1,\ldots,n\), with a fixed finite reported quantile set \(\mathcal T\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment with arms classified as Hall-heavy or finite-inverse-moment. Uniform assertions are restricted to laws separated from the phase boundary \(\gamma=2\) and to the learner schedules stated in the armwise theorems.
sampling_model.overlap: Positivity holds almost surely. Heavy arms have a common uniform second-order Hall lower-tail expansion. Finite-inverse-moment arms with finite \(\gamma_a\) inherit a uniform Lindeberg bound from the Hall tail and gamma separation, while \(\gamma_a=\infty\) arms have a common propensity lower bound from the fixed Hölder ball.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Each fold uses the constrained boundary-adapted Bernoulli series likelihood. The schedules retain \(J_N\log N/N\to0\) and \(J_N^{-s}\log(N/J_N)\to0\) at \(N=n\) and every refit size \(N=m\). Generalized-inverse scales, order-statistic clips, Hill classification, preliminary quantiles, endpoint scores, drift corrections, and densities are recomputed within each relevant sample.

prose_updates.related_work: Avella-Medina, Davis, and Samorodnitsky (2025, arXiv:2506.18215v1) provide the observed-true-propensity fixed-quantile benchmark but no feasible propensity-estimation theorem. The present class \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm S}\) is not literally their published class: it is narrower through its smooth one-dimensional boundary chart and uniform second-order Hall structure, but weaker, and therefore incomparable overall, in requiring only convergence of the finite nested quantile-score vector rather than a full conditional endpoint outcome law. The finite-\(\mathcal T\) oracle law is rederived using score-law factorization, not inherited through class inclusion. Hirano, Imbens, and Ridder (2003) motivate regular growing-likelihood projection; the proof here adds singular boundary information geometry and a uniform signed Riesz expansion. Firpo (2007) supplies regular QTE context, while the Gaussian branch here permits finite inverse moments and retains shared first-stage covariance. Heiler and Kazak (2021) motivate irregular subsampling, whereas the proved procedure refits both arm estimators and uses full-sample arm weights to recover the moving row law.
prose_updates.interpretation: For a varying law \(P\), the inferential object is the moving variable \(Z_{P,n}\), not a single universal weak limit. Fixed unequal heavy-tail indices produce asymptotic dominance by the smaller index, whereas gaps of order \(1/\log n\) keep both arms visible with row-dependent weights. Arm-vector refitting estimates the arm fluctuations at their own subsample scales and restores the full-sample weights, exactly reproducing the row-specific mixture.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The uniform theory excludes a neighborhood of \(\gamma_a=2\), uses a fixed finite quantile set, and is proved on the boundary-smooth class rather than the unrestricted Hall class. That class is narrower than the oracle anchor in chart smoothness and uniform second-order tails but incomparable in endpoint outcomes because only the finite score-vector law is controlled. The approximation-tail conditions are imposed at both full and refitted sample sizes. Coverage is pointwise in each reported quantile, with uniform convergence of finitely many coordinatewise errors, not simultaneous-band coverage. Anti-concentration is assumed directly for the moving row-law family. The critical fold-labelled point-process law is not asserted here.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The contribution is feasible uniform row-wise transfer and inference on the explicitly gamma-separated scheduled domain: the constrained likelihood has the displayed signed-functional rate and corrected amplified condition; the positive-weight estimator has a compensated heavy-arm law; the finite-variance estimator has the learned-propensity influence function and a Hall-derived uniform Lindeberg bound; and the normalized QTE is uniformly bounded-Lipschitz close to \(\mathcal L_P(Z_{P,n})\). Fully refitted arm-vector subsampling consistently estimates the same moving law and gives uniform pointwise coverage under the exact moving-law anti-concentration assumption. The \(1/\log n\) example refutes only approximation by fixed limiting mixtures and explains failure of raw scalar subsampling; it does not refute the arm-vector procedure. No claim is made at \(\gamma=2\), for an infinite quantile process, or for the separate critical fold-law question.

statement_notes.justification: It converts the oracle heavy-tail benchmark into a feasible growing-sieve theorem and proves uniform bounded-Lipschitz approximation to each gamma-separated row's compensated Lévy law.
statement_notes.gap: The observed-true-propensity benchmark does not establish learned-propensity transfer or the corrected amplified condition \(E_{a,n}M_n^{\gamma_a-1}=o_P(1)\).
statement_notes.consumer: It supplies the uniformly controlled irregular arm coordinate used by the moving QTE row law and refitted inference.

statement_notes.justification: The likelihood Riesz projection produces the learned-propensity score contribution, while Hall tails and the bounded-propensity Hölder branch verify uniform Lindeberg rather than assume it.
statement_notes.gap: Regular QTE theory does not provide this finite-inverse-moment profiled-sieve expansion with the data-driven clipping rule, a uniform asymptotic remainder, and row-specific Gaussian approximation.
statement_notes.consumer: It supplies the regular coordinate and shared cross-arm covariance in mixed and two-Gaussian moving row laws.

statement_notes.justification: The exact arm-scale identity and uniform joint arm expansion prove bounded-Lipschitz approximation to \(\mathcal L_P(Z_{P,n})\) without requiring the arm weights to converge.
statement_notes.gap: The oracle benchmark does not combine two learned convex arm estimators under unequal and locally varying normalizations.
statement_notes.consumer: It supplies the moving row distribution that valid refitted inference must reproduce.

statement_notes.justification: A complete-subsample variance calculation, uniform refitted arm expansions, negligible full-sample centering, and full-sample recombination prove conditional approximation to the moving row law.
statement_notes.gap: Raw scalar irregular subsampling changes the two-arm mixture under local \(1/\log n\) tail-index gaps; this is a fixed-limit/raw-method failure, not a failure of arm-vector moving-law inference.
statement_notes.consumer: It yields implementable pointwise confidence intervals with coverage uniform over the declared gamma-separated scheduled class.
